requirement: Typer CLI pipeline command with strict exception handling and distinct process exit codes (0 for success, 1 for missing artifact, 2 for validation error, 3 for runtime failure), logging errors to stderr.
skeleton: Typer app with deploy command executing deployment and mapping exceptions to typer.Exit codes and stderr logs.
caption: A Typer command-line application that turns each failure class into its own process exit code and writes every error to stderr. The module creates app as a typer.Typer with a no-op callback so it behaves as a multi-command CLI. execute_deployment(artifact_path, target_env) raises FileNotFoundError when the artifact does not exist, ValueError when the environment is neither staging nor production, and RuntimeError when the artifact's text content is empty, and otherwise returns a dictionary with status deployed, the environment, and the artifact file name. The deploy command takes a required --artifact option, short form -a, and an --env option, short form -e, defaulting to staging. It calls execute_deployment and echoes a SUCCESS line naming the artifact and environment, leaving the default exit code 0. A FileNotFoundError is printed as an Error line to stderr in red and converted into typer.Exit with code 1, a ValueError into a Validation Error line and code 2, and a RuntimeError into a Deployment Failed line and code 3; an Exit already in flight is re-raised unchanged, and no raw traceback reaches the user. The fixture drives the command through Typer's CliRunner and asserts exit 0 with SUCCESS: app.tar.gz deployed to staging on stdout, exit 1 with the not-found message on stderr and not on stdout, exit 2 with a Validation Error on stderr, and exit 3 with the empty-payload message on stderr and no Traceback text.

rationale.teaches: A Typer command that maps each failure class to a distinct exit code through typer.Exit and writes errors to stderr.
rationale.why: A CLI that prints the error and exits 0 looks fine in a terminal and breaks every script that checks the exit code. The fixture runs the command through CliRunner and asserts the code and the stream.

candidates.why_wrong: The missing-artifact branch prints but never raises typer.Exit, so the command exits 0.
The existence check is inverted, so an existing artifact is reported missing and a missing one proceeds.
A runtime failure re-raises the raw exception, so the user sees a traceback and the exit code is not 3.
A validation error exits with code 1, which the contract reserves for a missing artifact.
The error message is written to stdout, so scripts capturing stdout receive it as data.
